subtitulo: How to leave so that you are invited back — and the short list you can carry in a pocket when everything else has gone
cena: You have your bag on your shoulder and the door in sight, and there are nine people in this room who each need saying goodbye to individually.
frasePiso: Leave slowly, name one specific thing, and say a real see-you. That is the whole difference between a visit and a friendship.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: In Mexican social settings it is expected to greet and take leave of each person individually rather than addressing the group as a whole, and goodbyes are often prolonged; a hasty exit can imply the guest did not enjoy themselves.
fatosDatados.fonte: Consenso de fontes de etiqueta (Cultural Atlas — «Mexican Culture: Etiquette»; guias culturais convergentes)

steps.pt: Last part. The goodbye is not admin — it decides whether there is a next time, and it takes longer than you think.
Bag on your shoulder, door in sight, nine people in the room. In some countries you'd wave from the doorway. Not here.
Leaving already? Stay a little longer.
You say goodbye to each person, not to the room. That first quédate is ritual: you needn't stay, but don't sprint.

steps.promptPt: Decline the extra time warmly, without treating it as a real question. Speak now.
steps.es: Ya me tengo que ir, pero qué rico estuvo.
steps.pinyin: yah meh TEN-goh keh eer, PEH-roh keh RREE-koh ehs-TOO-boh
steps.pt: I have to go, but it was lovely.
steps.tts: Ya me tengo que ir, pero qué rico estuvo.

steps.pt: Now the move that gets you invited back, and it is one sentence: name a specific thing. Not it was lovely — which thing.

steps.promptPt: Name the one thing you'll actually remember from tonight. Speak now.
steps.es: El mole de tu mamá no se me va a olvidar.
steps.pinyin: el MOH-leh deh too mah-MAH noh seh meh bah ah ohl-bee-DAHR
steps.pt: I'm not going to forget your mum's mole.
steps.tts: El mole de tu mamá no se me va a olvidar.

steps.es: Le voy a decir, se va a poner contenta.
steps.pt: I'll tell her, she'll be pleased.
steps.tts: Le voy a decir, se va a poner contenta.

steps.pt: That sentence just travelled to someone not in the room. Specific praise moves through a family; generic praise stops.

steps.promptPt: Propose a next time that costs them nothing, so it isn't just politeness. Speak now.
steps.es: La próxima vez me toca a mí invitar.
steps.pinyin: lah PROK-see-mah behs meh TOH-kah ah mee een-bee-TAHR
steps.pt: Next time it's my turn to invite you.
steps.tts: La próxima vez me toca a mí invitar.

steps.pt: And the sign-off itself. Hasta luego works everywhere, but cuídate is warmer and it's what people use with someone they like.

steps.promptPt: Close it with the warm version, person to person. Speak now.
steps.pt: Take care. We'll be seeing each other.

steps.es: Que te vaya muy bien. Aquí tienes tu casa.
steps.pt: Safe travels. You have a home here.
steps.tts: Que te vaya muy bien. Aquí tienes tu casa.

steps.pt: Aquí tienes tu casa is not a figure of speech to wave away. Answer it properly and the door stays open.

steps.promptPt: Take the offer seriously in your answer. Speak now.
steps.es: Gracias, y ya sabes dónde tienes la tuya.
steps.pinyin: GRAH-syahs, ee yah SAH-behs DOHN-deh TYEH-nehs lah TOO-yah
steps.pt: Thank you — and you know where yours is.
steps.tts: Gracias, y ya sabes dónde tienes la tuya.

steps.pt: The pocket list: buenos días, con permiso, ¿me puede repetir?, ¿cuánto cuesta?, la cuenta por favor, muchas gracias.

steps.es: Ya me tengo que ir, pero qué rico estuvo. La próxima vez me toca a mí invitar. Cuídate mucho.
steps.pinyin: yah meh TEN-goh keh eer, PEH-roh keh RREE-koh ehs-TOO-boh. lah PROK-see-mah behs meh TOH-kah ah mee een-bee-TAHR. KWEE-dah-teh MOO-choh
steps.pt: Shadow the whole exit: the warm decline, the return invitation, the sign-off.
steps.tts: Ya me tengo que ir, pero qué rico estuvo. La próxima vez me toca a mí invitar. Cuídate mucho.

steps.pt: A08 complete, and the course with it. Each person, one specific thing, the next round, and cuídate. That gets you back.

aprofundar.titulo: Leaving is the part that decides the next time

secoes.titulo: Person by person, not room by room
secoes.corpo: Addressing the group and heading for the door is the single most common visitor misfire at the end of an evening. Each person gets a goodbye, and in most settings a handshake, a hug or a cheek kiss goes with it.
The first invitation to stay is part of the leaving ritual rather than a negotiation. You are not required to stay; you are required not to sprint. Slow down, answer it warmly, and continue leaving.
«It was lovely» stops at the person you said it to. «Your mum's mole» gets repeated to your mum. Naming one concrete thing is the difference between a polite guest and a guest somebody wants back.

If the whole course drains out of your head on the flight, six things survive and they are enough to be treated well anywhere: buenos días on the way in, con permiso to move past somebody, ¿me puede repetir? when you lose the thread, ¿cuánto cuesta? before you commit, la cuenta por favor to close, and muchas gracias on the way out.

permissao: You are allowed to take five minutes to leave. The long goodbye is not you failing to escape — it is the part of the evening where people tell each other it mattered, and hurrying it is the one thing that reads as ingratitude.
espelho: Anybody who has hosted knows the difference between the guest who waved from the door and the guest who found you in the kitchen to say thank you for the specific thing you'd worried about all afternoon. You have been on the hosting side of that; A08 is just asking you to be the second guest, in Spanish.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You announce that you're leaving, everyone says quédate otro ratito, and you're not sure whether they mean it or whether you've been rude to try to go.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: Either they genuinely want me to stay and leaving now is rude, or they're being polite and I should just go quickly.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The first invitation to stay is part of the leaving ritual rather than a real negotiation — it marks that your presence was welcome. Neither reading is right: you are not obliged to stay, and you are not free to leave in the next ten seconds either.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer it warmly, say you have to go, and then take a few minutes actually leaving — person by person, with one specific thing you enjoyed.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You exit as somebody who valued the evening rather than somebody who was waiting for a gap, which is the whole difference at invitation time.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not when the host is visibly winding down — clearing plates, checking the time, walking you toward the door. Then the ritual has already been closed by them and lingering becomes its own imposition.

fichasCulturais.sinal: As you go, someone says aquí tienes tu casa, and you smile and say thank you the way you'd handle any pleasantry.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: That's a set phrase, like 'take care' — nice, but not something anyone means literally.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: It is a set phrase and it is also a genuine offer of standing: it says the door is open to you specifically. Treating it as pure formula is not offensive, but it leaves the offer unanswered, and an unanswered offer quietly closes.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer in kind — thank them and tell them they have the same with you. It costs one sentence and it converts a courtesy into a relationship.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You end up with somewhere to come back to, which is the actual product of a good goodbye.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not with someone you have just met in a purely commercial exchange — a shopkeeper saying it warmly is being gracious, and matching it with an offer of your own home would overshoot.
